meta.about: Incorporated in 2010, Eternal Limited (previously Zomato Limited) is one of the leading online Food Service platforms in terms of the value of food sold. Its offerings include food delivery, dining-out services, Loyalty programs, and others. As of December 31, 2020, Eternal has established a strong footprint across 23 countries with 131,233 active food delivery restaurants, 161,637 active delivery partners, and an average monthly food order of 10.7 million customers.[1]

assumptions._note: Segment-driven model (as SWIGGY): each business's driver (net order value, NOV, or revenue) grows; adjusted revenue and adjusted EBITDA are % of the driver. A negative 'reconciliation' segment turns adjusted revenue into reported revenue. Consolidated reported EBITDA = sum of segment adjusted EBITDA − ESOP + Ind AS 116 rent add-back. Valued on sum of the parts on Sep-28E (roll FY28E/FY29E 50:50). ₹ crore.

segments.name: Food delivery (Zomato)
segments._why: NOV growth accelerated for four quarters to +20.1% YoY in Q1FY27 (+13.1% in Q1FY26). We hold ~20% in FY27E and fade to 17-18% as the base grows and Swiggy's Toing and Rapido's Ownly compete on price.
segments._revWhy: Adjusted revenue (commission, delivery and platform fees, ads) was 30.8% of NOV in FY26 and 32.8% in Q1FY27; we assume a slight further rise.
segments._marginWhy: Adjusted EBITDA 5.3% of NOV in FY26 and 5.6% in Q1FY27, near the top of management's 5-6% steady-state range; we assume 5.6-5.9%.

segments.name: Quick commerce (Blinkit)
segments._why: NOV +86% YoY in Q1FY27 (+19% QoQ, 200 net new stores to 2,443). The Q4FY26 letter guides NOV growth 'north of 60%' a year for three years; we use 72% / 55% / 45% (about 57% a year), a little below guidance because competition was at its peak in Q1.
segments._revWhy: Blinkit owns its inventory (1P) since Q2FY26, so revenue includes the full sale value: 92% of NOV in Q4FY26 and 91.4% in Q1FY27.
segments._marginWhy: Adjusted EBITDA improved for five quarters to 0.6% of NOV in Q1FY27 (−1.8% in Q1FY26). Management's steady state is 6% (raised to the top of the 5-6% range in Q1FY27). We assume 1.0% / 2.2% / 3.4%: about 1.2pp a year, well short of 6% by FY29E, because Q1FY27 was the peak of competitive intensity so far and new stores dilute margins (Nomura forecasts 0.9-2% for FY27-28).

segments.name: Going-out (District)
segments._why: NOV +59.8% YoY in Q1FY27; management targets US$3bn NOV by FY30 (30%+ growth a year). We assume 40% / 35% / 30%.
segments._revWhy: Revenue was 10.4% of NOV in FY26 and 9.9% in Q1FY27.
segments._marginWhy: Losses narrowed from −4.7% of NOV in Q3FY26 to −2.0% in Q1FY27; we assume breakeven during FY29E.

segments.name: B2B supplies (Hyperpure)
segments._why: FY26 revenue includes Q1FY26 (₹2,295 cr) before quick-commerce sellers' supplies moved inside Blinkit; the run-rate since is ~₹1,000 cr a quarter (Q1FY27 ₹1,034 cr, +27% YoY like-for-like). FY27E ~₹4,400 cr, then 22-25% growth in restaurant supplies.
segments._marginWhy: Adjusted EBITDA 0.6% of revenue in Q1FY27 (−0.8% a year earlier); a thin-margin distribution business.

segments.name: Others (Bistro, Nugget, new bets)
segments._why: Bistro (10-minute food) and Nugget (AI customer support) are scaling: adjusted revenue ₹95 cr in Q1FY27 vs ₹4 cr a year earlier.
segments._marginWhy: Loss of ₹94 cr in Q1FY27 (₹215 cr in FY26); we assume ~₹400 cr of losses in FY27E, roughly flat in rupees after that as revenue scales.

segments.name: Adjusted-to-reported revenue reconciliation
segments._why: Adjusted revenue adds food-delivery customer charges and platform fees that are not in reported revenue: −₹1,539 cr in FY26, −₹437 cr in Q1FY27. Grows with food NOV; no effect on EBITDA.
segments._revWhy: Driver is the reconciling amount itself.

assumptions._unallocLabel: Ind AS 116 rent add-back (negative = raises reported EBITDA)
assumptions._unallocWhy: Segment adjusted EBITDA is after rent on leased stores, warehouses and offices; reported EBITDA moves rent below EBITDA (into depreciation and interest). FY26 ₹838 cr; Q1FY27 ₹294 cr (₹1,180 cr annualised) and rising with ~800 new Blinkit stores a year.
assumptions._esopWhy: Share-based pay: ₹798 cr FY25, ₹819 cr FY26, ₹255 cr in Q1FY27 (₹1,020 cr annualised). Non-cash, but it dilutes shareholders.
assumptions._capexWhy: Cash capex ₹1,746 cr in FY26 and ₹711 cr in Q1FY27 (stores and warehouses; ~₹2.5 cr per store including warehousing, ~800 stores a year) gives ~₹2,800 cr in FY27E, plus ~₹600 cr of lease principal, because reported EBITDA excludes rent.
assumptions._depWhy: Depreciation (including right-of-use assets) ₹1,597 cr in FY26 and ₹546 cr in Q1FY27 (₹2,180 cr annualised, rising with stores).
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Other income ₹1,396 cr in FY26 and ₹1,417 cr TTM to Q1FY27 on ~₹18,000 cr of company cash (≈7.7%, including mark-to-market gains on debt funds). The model's treasury is net of ₹4,592 cr of lease liabilities, so we take 7.5% on net treasury plus 7.5% on the cash matched to leases (₹345 cr, 'otherIncome').
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: 7.5% on the ₹4,592 cr of cash that matches lease liabilities (Mar-26), which the model nets off treasury.
assumptions._interestWhy: Finance cost ₹392 cr FY26, ₹151 cr in Q1FY27; almost all interest on leases, rising with stores. There is no bank debt.
assumptions._taxWhy: Q1FY27 tax was ₹180 cr on ₹272 cr of PBT (66%): the parent's carried-forward losses run out in FY27, so food-delivery and treasury income are taxed at ~25% while losses in the Blinkit, District and Hyperpure subsidiaries cannot be offset. From FY28E Blinkit's profits are sheltered by its own past losses, so the group rate falls to ~25%.

otherTreasury.label: Bank deposits held in other financial assets (treasury)
otherTreasury._why: Company-reported cash balance ₹17,972 cr at Mar-26 less ₹16,356 cr shown as cash and investments on the balance sheet.

dcf._betaWhy: Long-duration, high-growth consumer internet stock; above-market sensitivity (cost of equity 13.1%). No debt other than leases, so cost of equity = WACC.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~40% (FY29E) to 9% by year 15 as quick commerce matures.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 8.5% reported EBITDA margin on 1P revenue: Blinkit at its 6% of NOV steady state (~6.6% of revenue, ~85% of group revenue) and food at ~18% of food revenue, plus the rent add-back less ESOP cost.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Store and warehouse capex plus lease principal settle at ~2.5% of revenue (Blinkit spends 6.3% of a new store's NOV on capex; maintenance and slower store additions at maturity).

parts.name: Quick commerce (Blinkit)

NOV (order value) rather than EBITDA because Blinkit earns 1-3% of NOV today, so an EBITDA multiple swings wildly; this matches how we value Swiggy's Instamart (EV/GOV).

parts.note: Start-up losses (Bistro, Nugget) valued as the cost still to come: three years of FY28E losses (bull: one year; bear: five), as for Swiggy's new bets.

parts.name: Net cash at end-FY27E (after leases)
parts.note: Model forecast: cash + investments + deposits − lease liabilities at Mar-27.

parts.name: Add back lease liabilities
parts.metricLabel: Rent is already deducted in segment EBITDA
parts.note: Lease liabilities (₹4,592 cr, Mar-26) are store and warehouse rent obligations; segment EBITDA is after rent, so deducting them again would double count (as in our Swiggy SOTP).

methods.name: Sum of the parts
methods.why: Four businesses at different stages (profitable food, just-profitable quick commerce, loss-making going-out and new bets) each need their own yardstick. The street's method. Primary.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Whole-company cash flows over 15 years at a 13.1% cost of equity; tests whether the parts add up to a credible cash-flow path.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Group Sep-28E reported EBITDA at the street's food multiple (37.5x): what the whole company is worth if every rupee of EBITDA earned the mature business's multiple. Bull 50x (Nuvama/Elara's Blinkit EBITDA multiples); bear 30x (our Swiggy food multiple).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Food keeps growing ~20% at ~6% margins and earns 42x; Blinkit grows ~65% a year, reaches ~4.6% of NOV by FY29E and is valued at 1.75x NOV (Emkay); District earns 0.9x NOV.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Price-led entrants slow food growth to ~14% and margins slip (30x, as for Swiggy); the quick-commerce price war keeps Blinkit's margin near 1-2% and growth slows to ~40% a year, so it is worth ~1x NOV; District breaks even two years later.

cover.headline: The best franchise in Indian consumer internet, fairly priced
cover.lead: Eternal owns India's #1 food-delivery app (Zomato), the #1 quick-commerce network (Blinkit), a going-out app (District) and a restaurant-supplies business (Hyperpure). At ₹{{P.last|num}} the stock is 8% below its 52-week high. Q1FY27 was strong: B2C order value +54%, food-delivery margin 5.6% of order value, and Blinkit profitable for a third quarter while adding 200 stores. But at a market value of ~₹3,08,812 cr the market already pays for most of the quick-commerce plan: valuing the other parts as we do, the price implies ~1.0x Blinkit's Sep-28E order value. Our sum of the parts gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}})**: **we initiate with HOLD.** Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}} ({{scen.bear.upside|chg}}).

arguments.h: Food delivery: the profitable leader, growing faster again
arguments.p: Zomato's NOV grew 20.1% in Q1FY27 (four quarters of acceleration) at a 5.6% margin, near the top of the 5-6% target. It is bigger, faster-growing and roughly twice as profitable as Swiggy's food business. Price-led entrants (Toing, Ownly) are the risk to watch.

arguments.h: Blinkit has won the quick-commerce scale race
arguments.p: NOV +86.2% to ₹17,132 cr, ~2.9x Instamart; 2,443 stores; adjusted EBITDA +₹102 cr while every rival loses money. Management raised the steady-state margin target to 6% of NOV. We assume only 3.4% by FY29E.

arguments.h: Self-funding, but profit is thin and the tax rate is rising
arguments.p: Cash rose to ₹18,288 cr in Q1FY27; the business now pays for its own stores and inventory. But reported profit is small (₹92 cr in Q1FY27) and tax jumped to 66% of profit before tax as the parent's past losses ran out. Our FY27E EPS ({{F.eps.0|n1}}) is well below consensus.

arguments.h: Valuation: fair, with Blinkit priced at ~1x order value
arguments.p: Our sum of the parts (food 37.5x Sep-28E EBITDA, the street's median; Blinkit 1.2x Sep-28E NOV, the median broker value) gives {{dcf.tp|inr}}, {{dcf.upside|chg}}: just short of our BUY line. Valuing the other parts as we do, the price implies ~1.0x Blinkit's NOV. The street's median target is ₹390.

sections.title: Four businesses on one delivery network

blocks.p: Eternal (called Zomato until 2025) runs consumer apps that connect customers with restaurants, stores and events, and delivers the order, usually in 10-30 minutes. Its headline measure is **net order value (NOV)**: the value of orders after discounts. In food delivery and going-out it earns a **take rate** (commissions, customer fees and advertising). In quick commerce it now buys and sells the goods itself (the **inventory or "1P" model**), so revenue there is close to the full sale value and margin is best read as a share of order value.

sections.title: Two markets: a profitable duopoly and a crowded race

blocks.p: **Food delivery** is a two-player market (Zomato and Swiggy) in which both now make money. Redseer: India's food-services market ~US$90bn in FY26, ~US$150bn by FY31; online delivery's share rises from 11% to 18%, i.e. 20-22% a year growth (IBEF, 9-Jul-2026). Zomato is the larger and more profitable player: in Q1FY27 its food NOV (₹10,769 cr) exceeded Swiggy's GOV (₹9,490 cr) even though NOV is the stricter measure, and it earned twice Swiggy's food profit. New price-led apps (Swiggy's Toing, Rapido's Ownly) are the first challenge to the duopoly's pricing in years.

**Quick commerce** (groceries and essentials in 10-20 minutes) is the growth market and far more crowded. Blinkit, Instamart and Zepto together hold ~90% of quick commerce; Flipkart Minutes, Amazon Now and BigBasket are in single digits each (Infisum via Business Today, 14-Sep-2026). Discounts eased to 19-20% of order value from 24-27% in Oct-25 to Mar-26 (UBS). Scale decides who makes money: a store breaks even only when it handles enough orders a day (~1,100-1,200 by Business Today's estimate), and Blinkit is the only major player that is profitable.

sections.title: Food delivery: growth re-accelerating at a 5.6% margin

blocks.p: Food delivery is the profit engine. Net order value rose from ₹32,862 cr in FY25 to ₹37,993 cr in FY26 (+16%) and adjusted EBITDA from ₹1,505 cr to ₹2,017 cr. Growth has accelerated for four straight quarters, from +13.1% in Q1FY26 to +20.1% in Q1FY27 (₹10,769 cr), driven by more customers (27.2 mn a month, up from 22.9 mn). Margin rose to 5.6% of NOV, near the top of management's 5-6% steady-state range. Contribution (profit after delivery costs and discounts, before fixed costs) is steady at ~10% of NOV, so the margin gain comes from spreading fixed costs over more orders.

blocks.p: **The new price fighters.** Swiggy launched Toing, a budget-meals app, and Rapido launched Ownly, both with lower restaurant commissions and delivery fees. Management says the impact has been "limited": the same restaurants, similar or longer delivery times and lower prices paid for by thinner economics. Its answer is Bistro (10-minute food at ₹50-150 from its own kitchens), reported under "Others". Zomato's Q1FY27 growth acceleration suggests the entrants have not dented it yet; the risk is that price-led entrants push the whole category's take rates down.

sections.title: Blinkit: the market leader, profitable and still growing ~86%

blocks.p: Blinkit delivers groceries and household goods in about ten minutes from 2,443 stores (Jun-2026). Order value more than doubled from ₹22,371 cr in FY25 to ₹48,568 cr in FY26, and reached ₹17,132 cr in Q1FY27 (+86.2% YoY, +19% QoQ). Since Q2FY26 Blinkit has owned its inventory (the 1P model, allowed once Eternal became Indian-owned and controlled), which raised gross profit to 27.5% of NOV. Adjusted EBITDA has improved for five quarters, from −₹162 cr in Q1FY26 to +₹102 cr in Q1FY27 (0.6% of NOV), while 900 stores were added in a year.

blocks.p: Two risks sit under these numbers. **Competition:** Q1FY27 was "the peak of competitive intensity" (CEO Albinder Dhindsa), with Zepto, Instamart, Flipkart Minutes, Amazon Now and BigBasket subsidising groceries and delivery fees; Blinkit says it will not match discount-led growth. **Capital intensity:** capex per store has risen to ₹2.5 cr and owning stock ties up working capital; inventory losses are ~1.8% of NOV. blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** Eternal has a **real scale advantage** in both its big markets: it is the larger, more profitable food-delivery network, and Blinkit has won the quick-commerce scale race (profitable while every rival loses money). That is a moat of scale and density, not of lock-in: customers can switch apps in seconds, and deep-pocketed rivals (Amazon, Flipkart, Reliance) can keep subsidising. The advantage is durable as long as Eternal keeps investing, which is why margins will rise more slowly than the order value.

sections.title: Revenue has jumped 27x in five years; profit is still thin

blocks.p: Eternal's reported revenue rose from ₹1,994 cr in FY21 to ₹54,364 cr in FY26. Two things drove it: food delivery kept growing (order value up ~80% from FY22 to FY25), and quick commerce (Blinkit, bought in 2022) grew into the largest business. The FY26 jump (+169%) is mostly an accounting change: from Q2FY26 Blinkit owns the goods it sells (the "1P" or inventory model), so revenue now includes the full sale value, not just a commission. The company turned profitable in FY24 (₹351 cr), but profit is small against a ~₹3 lakh crore market value: ₹366 cr in FY26 and ₹92 cr in Q1FY27, after a sharp rise in tax.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** reported margins look tiny (EBITDA 2.2% of revenue in FY26) because Blinkit's revenue is now gross sale value. The better yardstick is profit as a share of order value: adjusted EBITDA was 1.2% of B2C net order value in FY26 and 1.8% in Q1FY27. Depreciation nearly doubled in FY26 (₹863 cr → ₹1,597 cr) as stores and warehouses were added, and tax will take a larger bite from FY27 because the parent company's past losses are used up. The path from EBITDA to earnings per share is therefore slower than the order growth suggests.

sections.title: Reported vs adjusted profit: ESOPs, rent, tax and a change in revenue

blocks.p: Eternal's "adjusted EBITDA" and reported EBITDA happen to be close (₹1,189 cr vs ₹1,208 cr in FY26), but only because two large items cancel out. Share-based pay (ESOP, ₹819 cr) is left out of adjusted EBITDA, which flatters it; rent (₹838 cr) is counted in adjusted EBITDA but moved below EBITDA in the reported accounts, which flatters reported EBITDA. ESOP cost is real: it is paid in new shares, and the share count has risen every year.

bullets: **Revenue recognition changed in Q2FY26.** Once Blinkit began owning inventory, its revenue became the full sale value rather than a commission. Reported revenue grew 169% in FY26, but like-for-like growth was ~64%. Compare growth on order value, not revenue, and read margins as a share of NOV.

**Tax is stepping up.** Until FY26 Eternal paid tax mainly on treasury income. The parent company (which houses food delivery) uses up its carried-forward losses in FY27, so its business profit is now taxed, while the subsidiaries that run Blinkit, District and Hyperpure still carry losses that cannot be set off against it. Q1FY27 tax was ₹180 cr on profit before tax of ₹272 cr (66%). This is why profit fell in Q1FY27 even though EBITDA rose 29% QoQ.

**Other income is large and partly market-driven.** Treasury income was ₹1,396 cr in FY26, more than reported EBITDA, and includes mark-to-market gains on debt funds; the company's cash table counts only cash received (₹953 cr in FY26).

**Nothing is capitalised.** Management says all employee and technology costs are expensed above adjusted EBITDA (Q1FY27 letter). Inventory losses (~1.8% of quick-commerce NOV) are inside cost of goods sold.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** We see no sign of aggressive accounting, and the company reconciles every adjusted number. But large ESOPs paid in shares, a change in how Blinkit's revenue is booked, a rising tax rate and market-driven treasury income all make the headline numbers harder to read than the order-value story suggests.

sections.title: Cash: ₹18,288 cr, no debt, and the business now funds itself

blocks.p: Eternal holds ₹18,288 cr of cash and treasury investments (Jun-2026, company figure), built mostly from the IPO (Jul-2021) and an ₹8,500 cr share placement (QIP) in Nov-2024. It has no bank debt: the "borrowings" on the balance sheet (₹4,592 cr at Mar-26) are lease liabilities for stores, warehouses and offices. The cash pile has been broadly flat for a year (₹18,824 cr at Mar-25, ₹17,972 cr at Mar-26) because operating profit plus treasury income roughly paid for capex and the inventory that Blinkit now holds. Note that the company's own cash figure is higher than "cash + investments" below because ~₹1,600 cr of bank deposits sit inside other assets.
